items.title: Good morning The signaling accompanying the Bank of Japan's rate hike sent the Yen weaker: In a widely expected move, Japan’s central bank raised interest rates by 25 basis points to their highest level since 1995. Yet, as the signaling regarding future hikes disappointed markets, the Yen depreciated more than 1%, continuing to unwind gains sparked by (actual and anticipated) FX intervention. (CNBC chart below). #economy #markets j #japan #boj #centralbanks

items.title: Posted earlier: Depending on where you look, the current U.S. economy can be characterized in one of three ways: 1. An economy in equilibrium, anchored by forces of mean reversion. 2. An increasingly unstable equilibrium, driven by diminishing financial and physical buffers. 3. An economy in multi-year transition, reshaped by technological change and geo-economics. Rather than opting for just one of these, consider the world of the in-between:  #economy #markets @nytimes

items.title: Despite widespread analyst commentary today that the Federal Reserve addressed inflation concerns and passed a “credibility test,” longer-term yields have remained relatively range-bound over the last few days. This is not because those factors are unimportant, but because they have not been, and are not, the primary drivers pushing yields higher. #economy #markets @CNBC @cnbcclosingbell #federalreserve
